name: Pierce Brosnan
milestone_by_age_26: Fame arrived at age 29 with the TV series Remington Steele (1982); by 26 he was performing in London theatre productions (stage debut 1976, Roundhouse 1977) but had no material career milestone.
early_history_summary: Brosnan left school at 16 in London, trained in commercial illustration, then switched to acting at the Drama Centre London, graduating in 1975. He worked as a stage actor in provincial theatre and made his London debut in 1976, but his breakout came with Remington Steele in 1982 at age 29.
family_context_summary: Born in Drogheda, Ireland to a nurse and a carpenter who left the family when Pierce was an infant; raised by grandparents and then an aunt after his mother moved to London.
evidence_summary: Brosnan trained at the Drama Centre London and worked as a stage actor through his early twenties, but his career-defining role in Remington Steele came at 29 and James Bond at 42. No material milestone by 26 was found.

name: Denise Perrier
milestone_by_age_26: Won Miss World 1953 at age 18, becoming the first and only French woman to hold the title.
early_history_summary: Perrier grew up in Ambérieu-en-Bugey, France, and spent her teens in French Indochina where her father was a gendarme. While on vacation in the Côte d'Azur in 1953, a casino director spotted her and invited her to compete in Miss Saint-Raphaël that same night, which she won, leading to the Miss France World contest and ultimately the Miss World 1953 title in London.
family_context_summary: Born in Ambérieu-en-Bugey, France; her father was a gendarme and the family lived in French Indochina before returning to France around 1952.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; father was a military gendarme with no known connection to modeling or entertainment.
primary_early_advantage_tags: beauty pageant pipeline, physical appearance, casino director discovery
evidence_summary: Perrier was discovered by chance at 18 when a casino director invited her to compete in a local beauty pageant. She won Miss Saint-Raphaël, then Miss France World, and ultimately Miss World 1953 in London. Her father was a gendarme and the family had lived in French Indochina. No evidence of prior training or family connections in modeling or entertainment was found.
starting_point: Born in 1935 in Ambérieu-en-Bugey, France; father was a gendarme; family lived in French Indochina during her teens before returning to France around 1952.
current_position: Retired, living in Falicon near Nice, France; formerly served as municipal councilor in Nice; age 91 as of 2025.

trajectory.event: Won Miss World 1953 at the Lyceum Theatre in London, becoming the first and only French woman to hold the title.
Presented her first art exhibition, exploring painting alongside her modeling career.
Appeared as a Bond girl in the film Diamonds Are Forever alongside Sean Connery.
Became a municipal councilor in Nice under Mayor Jacques Médecin, serving three mandates.
Returned to judge the 60th Miss World finals and reminisced on her 1953 win.

name: Rainer Weiss
milestone_by_age_26: No material scientific milestone by 26; was an electronics technician and undergraduate student at MIT. Failed courses and left MIT as a student in 1953, worked as a lab technician, later completed SB in 1955 and PhD in 1962. Nobel Prize in Physics came in 2017 at age 85.
early_history_summary: Weiss fled Nazi Germany with his family to Prague and then the United States. He became fascinated with electronics as a teenager in New York, building high-fidelity equipment. He attended MIT but failed courses due to personal distractions, left school, and worked as an electronics technician in Jerrold Zacharias's lab before returning to complete his degree.
family_context_summary: Born in Berlin to a Jewish communist neurologist father and a Christian actress mother; family fled to Prague then the United States in 1939 with help from the Stix family of St. Louis.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a physician (neurologist); mother was an actress; family was intellectual but displaced by Nazi persecution.
evidence_summary: Weiss had an early interest in electronics and attended MIT, but failed courses and left school to work as a technician. He returned to complete his SB in 1955 and PhD in 1962. His major scientific contributions (LIGO, COBE, Nobel Prize) came decades later. No material milestone by 26 was found.

name: Steve Yzerman
milestone_by_age_26: Drafted 4th overall by the Detroit Red Wings in 1983 at age 18; scored 87 points (39 goals) as a rookie, named captain at 21, and won the Lester B. Pearson Trophy as NHL's most outstanding player at 24.
early_history_summary: Yzerman started hockey at age 5-7 in Cranbrook, BC, then moved to Nepean, Ontario at age 9 where he played for the Nepean Raiders peewee team. He joined the Peterborough Petes of the OHL at 16, was drafted 4th overall by Detroit in 1983, and immediately became an impact NHL player with 87 points as a rookie.
family_context_summary: Born in Cranbrook, BC to Ron and Jean Yzerman; father was passionate about hockey and enrolled Steve in a league a year above his age. Family moved to Nepean, Ontario when Steve was 9-10.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Ron Yzerman was a passionate hockey parent who instilled a love of the game; no evidence of professional hockey background in the family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Canadian junior hockey pipeline, OHL Peterborough Petes, early specialization, NHL draft, father hockey passion
evidence_summary: Yzerman grew up in a Canadian hockey family where his father enrolled him in leagues early. He played peewee hockey in Nepean, joined the OHL's Peterborough Petes at 16, and was drafted 4th overall by Detroit in 1983. He scored 87 points as an 18-year-old rookie, was named captain at 21, and won the Pearson Trophy at 24. The Canadian junior hockey pipeline (Nepean Raiders → OHL → NHL) was the dominant early advantage.
starting_point: Born in 1965 in Cranbrook, BC, Canada to Ron and Jean Yzerman; father was a passionate hockey parent who enrolled Steve in leagues before age 6; family moved to Nepean, Ontario when Steve was 9.
current_position: Executive vice president and general manager of the Detroit Red Wings; inducted into Hockey Hall of Fame in 2009; net worth estimated in the tens of millions.

trajectory.event: Drafted 4th overall by the Detroit Red Wings; scored 39 goals and 87 points as a rookie, finishing second in Calder Trophy voting.
Named captain of the Detroit Red Wings, the youngest captain in franchise history at the time.
Won the Lester B. Pearson Trophy as the NHL's most outstanding player after a 155-point season.
Led the Red Wings to their first Stanley Cup championship in 42 years.
Won Olympic gold medal with Team Canada at the Salt Lake City Winter Olympics.
Retired after 22 NHL seasons with 692 goals and 1,755 career points.
Inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in his first year of eligibility.

name: Jonas Eriksson
milestone_by_age_26: Became an Allsvenskan (top Swedish league) referee around 2000 at age 26, but major refereeing achievements (FIFA listed 2002, World Cup 2014, Europa League final 2016) all came after age 26.
early_history_summary: Eriksson started refereeing at age 13 in his hometown of Luleå, Sweden, became a professional referee in 1994 at 20, and was promoted to the Allsvenskan in 2000. He also built a business career alongside refereeing, becoming financially independent after selling his stake in IEC Sports in 2007.
family_context_summary: Born and raised in Luleå, Sweden; started his own sports club at age 8 and became a child reporter at age 12, showing early entrepreneurial drive.
evidence_summary: Eriksson began refereeing at 13 and reached the Allsvenskan by 26, but his significant achievements (FIFA listing, World Cup, Europa League final) all came after age 26. He also became a millionaire through his business career at IEC Sports. No material milestone by 26 was found beyond reaching the top domestic league, which is borderline.

name: Orhan Pamuk
milestone_by_age_26: No published novel or literary award by 26; he began writing his first novel at 22 and finished it around 26, but it was not published until 1982 when he was 30. His first contest win (Milliyet Press Novel Contest) came in 1979 at age 27.
early_history_summary: Pamuk grew up in a wealthy but declining upper-class family in Istanbul's Nişantaşı district. He was educated at Robert College, studied architecture for three years, then switched to journalism. He started writing his first novel at 22 and devoted himself to writing, but success came slowly with his first novel not published until he was 30.
family_context_summary: Born into a prosperous, secular upper-middle-class Istanbul family; grandfather was a successful civil engineer and businessman who founded the family fortune; father was an engineer who kept losing money.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family of engineers and businessmen; grandfather founded the family fortune through railroad and factory construction. No direct literary tradition in the family.
evidence_summary: Pamuk grew up in a wealthy Istanbul family, attended Robert College, and studied architecture before switching to writing. He started his first novel at 22 and lived with his mother while writing for years. His first contest win came at 27 and first publication at 30. No material milestone by 26 was found.

name: Hana Brady
milestone_by_age_26: Murdered at Auschwitz at age 13 in 1944; achieved no milestones during her short life. Her story became known through the 2002 book Hana's Suitcase, making her fame entirely posthumous.
early_history_summary: Hana Brady was a Czechoslovak Jewish girl from Nové Město na Moravě. She was separated from her parents by the Nazis, sent to Theresienstadt concentration camp, and murdered in the gas chambers at Auschwitz on October 23, 1944 at age 13. Her story became widely known decades later through the children's book Hana's Suitcase.
family_context_summary: Born to Karel and Markéta Brady in Nové Město na Moravě, Czechoslovakia; the family ran a store and was one of the few Jewish families in the town, initially well-integrated into local life.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family operated a store in their small town; father was involved in local community life as a soccer team captain and volunteer fireman. No domain-specific advantage relevant to later fame.
evidence_summary: Hana Brady was a child murdered in the Holocaust at age 13. She had no opportunity for any achievement or milestone. Her fame is entirely posthumous, resulting from the 2002 book Hana's Suitcase. She is not a valid candidate for success-by-26 analysis.

name: Arunachalam Muruganantham
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by 26; he was working as a machine tool operator, farm laborer, and welder after dropping out of school at 14. His invention of the low-cost sanitary pad-making machine came around 2004-2006 at age 43-45.
early_history_summary: Muruganantham grew up in poverty near Coimbatore, India, after his father died in a road accident. He dropped out of school at 14 and worked various manual jobs. He married in 1998 at age 37 and began working on sanitary pad innovation after discovering his wife used rags, eventually inventing a low-cost pad-making machine.
family_context_summary: Born into poverty in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu; father died in a road accident when Muruganantham was young; mother worked as a farm laborer. He dropped out of school at 14 to support the family.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; family was impoverished with no relevant domain expertise.
evidence_summary: Muruganantham grew up in severe poverty, dropped out of school at 14, and worked manual labor jobs through his twenties. His invention of the low-cost sanitary pad-making machine came in his late thirties to forties after his 1998 marriage. He received the Padma Shri in 2016. No material milestone by 26 was found.

name: Pyotr Klimuk
milestone_by_age_26: Selected as a cosmonaut in 1965 at age 23 and completed basic training by 25, but his first spaceflight (Soyuz 13) did not occur until December 1973 at age 31. No material achievement milestone by 26.
early_history_summary: Klimuk was born to a peasant family in Komarovka, Belarus; his father was lost in World War II. He graduated from an aviation school in 1964 and was selected for the Soviet cosmonaut program in 1965. He completed basic training by 1967 but waited years for his first spaceflight assignment.
family_context_summary: Born to a peasant family in Komarovka, Brest region, Belarus; father was lost in 1944 during World War II. Grew up in post-war rural poverty.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; family was rural peasant with no aviation or military tradition noted.
evidence_summary: Klimuk came from a peasant family in Belarus, graduated from aviation school in 1964, and was selected as a cosmonaut in 1965. While selection into the cosmonaut corps is notable, his first actual spaceflight did not occur until 1973 at age 31. No material achievement milestone by 26 was found.

name: Dimosthenis Tampakos
milestone_by_age_26: Won bronze at the 1998 European Championships at age 22, bronze at the 1999 World Championships at 23, and Olympic silver plus European gold at the 2000 Olympics/European Championships at age 24.
early_history_summary: Tampakos started gymnastics at age 8 in Kalamaria, Thessaloniki, and joined Spartakos Thessaloniki within a year. He competed in his first meet at age 9. He was coached by Alex Ioakimidis and specialized in the rings, where he introduced an original move in 1997. His first major international medal came at the 1998 European Championships.
family_context_summary: Born in Thessaloniki; father Christos worked for the Greek air force, mother Irini was a stay-at-home mom. He lived with his parents through his athletic career, providing a stable environment.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family background in gymnastics; parents enrolled him in gymnastics because he could not stay still as a child.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early gymnastics specialization, Spartakos club, coach Ioakimidis, stable family, rings specialization
evidence_summary: Tampakos began gymnastics at 8 in Thessaloniki and joined Spartakos club, where he was coached by Alex Ioakimidis. He was a methodical, slow worker who specialized in the rings and introduced an original move in 1997. His father's air force job provided a stable middle-class background. He won his first major international medal at 22 (European Championships bronze) and went on to win Olympic silver and European gold at 24.
starting_point: Born in 1976 in Thessaloniki, Greece; father worked for the Greek air force, mother was a stay-at-home mom; started gymnastics at age 8 because he could not stay still as a child.
current_position: Wing Commander in the Greek Air Force and Head of the Planning and Research Office at the Supreme Council of Armed Forces Sports; President of the National Olympic Academy; residing in Greece.

trajectory.event: Introduced an original move on the rings (cross to inverted cross with fully extended body) and won bronze at the Mediterranean Games in Bari.
Won bronze medal at the European Championships in Saint Petersburg on the rings.
Won bronze medal at the World Championships in Tianjin on the rings.
Won Olympic silver at Sydney and European gold at Bremen on the rings.
Tied for gold at the World Championships in Anaheim on the rings.
Won Olympic gold medal on the rings at the Athens Olympics with a score of 9.862, serving as Greek flagbearer at the opening ceremony.

name: Antonio Carlos Ortega
milestone_by_age_26: Helped CB Maristas Málaga win promotion to the Liga ASOBAL (top Spanish division) at 19 in 1990, then joined FC Barcelona at 23 and won multiple EHF Champions League titles (1996, 1997) by age 26.
early_history_summary: Ortega started playing handball at age 8 at the Maristas school in Málaga, where teachers were the coaches. He played through all youth categories and entered the first team at 18, helping the club win promotion to the top Spanish division. He was twice top scorer in Spain before joining FC Barcelona in 1994 at age 23, where he became part of the legendary Dream Team.
family_context_summary: Born in Málaga, Spain; no specific family background documented beyond growing up in the Maristas school community where handball was a major activity.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family handball connections.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Maristas school handball program, FC Barcelona Dream Team, Spanish handball dominance, early specialization, coach Valero Rivera
evidence_summary: Ortega began handball at 8 at the Maristas school in Málaga, playing there for 15 years and helping the club reach the top Spanish division at 18. He was twice top scorer in Spain before joining FC Barcelona at 23, where he won multiple Champions League titles as part of the Dream Team. The Maristas school program and the FC Barcelona pipeline were the dominant early advantages. His club's sponsor going bankrupt forced his move to Barcelona.
starting_point: Born in 1971 in Málaga, Spain; began playing handball at age 8 at the Maristas school where the sport was a major extracurricular activity.
current_position: Head coach of FC Barcelona handball team since 2021; has won multiple titles including the EHF Champions League as coach; resides in the Barcelona area.

trajectory.event: Helped CB Maristas Málaga win promotion to the Liga ASOBAL, Spain's top handball division.
Joined FC Barcelona, beginning an 11-year playing career with the club's legendary Dream Team.
Won the first of six EHF Champions League titles with FC Barcelona.
Won Olympic bronze medal with the Spanish national team at the Sydney Olympics.
Retired as a player due to a knee injury, transitioning to coaching.
Became head coach of FC Barcelona handball, winning the EHF Champions League in his first season.

name: Li Na
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 2004 Guangzhou International Women's Open at age 22, becoming the first Chinese player to win a WTA Tour singles title; reached the Wimbledon quarterfinals in 2006 at age 24, the first Chinese player to do so.
early_history_summary: Li Na started badminton at age 6 in Wuhan, following her father's footsteps, but was switched to tennis at age 8 after coaches noticed her swing. She joined China's national tennis team at 15, was sent to the John Newcombe Academy in Texas at 15 (sponsored by Nike), and turned professional at 17. She briefly left tennis in 2002 to study at university before returning in 2004 to win her first WTA title.
family_context_summary: Born in Wuhan, China to an amateur badminton player father who died of cardiovascular disease when Li was 14, and a mother she felt responsible to support. The family was not wealthy, and tennis was virtually unknown in China at the time.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an amateur badminton player who steered Li into sports; no professional sports background in the family. Father's death when Li was 14 created urgency for her to succeed.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Chinese state sports system, national tennis team, John Newcombe Academy, Nike sponsorship, father badminton influence, father's death urgency
evidence_summary: Li Na grew up in Wuhan with an amateur badminton player father who steered her into sports. She switched to tennis at 8, joined the national team at 15, and was sent to the John Newcombe Academy in Texas on a Nike sponsorship. The Chinese state sports system was the dominant early advantage, providing training, facilities, and international exposure. Her father's death at 14 created urgency. She won her first WTA title at 22, becoming the first Chinese WTA champion.
starting_point: Born in 1982 in Wuhan, China to an amateur badminton player father and a mother; father died of cardiovascular disease when Li was 14, creating financial pressure and urgency to succeed in tennis.
current_position: Retired from professional tennis since 2014; living in Wuhan, China; inducted into International Tennis Hall of Fame in 2019; estimated career prize money of $16.7 million.

trajectory.event: Turned professional and won her first ITF circuit titles.
Won the Guangzhou International Women's Open, becoming the first Chinese player to win a WTA Tour singles title.
Reached the Wimbledon quarterfinals, the first Chinese player to reach a Grand Slam singles quarterfinal.
Parted ways with the Chinese state sports system to operate independently, keeping more of her prize money.
Won the French Open, becoming the first Asian-born player to win a Grand Slam singles title.
Won the Australian Open and reached a career-high world No. 2 ranking before retiring in September 2014.
Inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame.
